title: A Kingfisher's Beak Fixed Japan's Bullet Train

scenes.text: Japan's bullet train was copied from a bird's beak.
It used to blast a loud sonic boom out of tunnels, heard 400 meters away.
An engineer who loved birdwatching noticed how a kingfisher dives into water with barely a splash.
He copied the beak for the train's nose.
The train got ten percent faster and used fifteen percent less electricity.

description:
Japan's Shinkansen created a loud boom when it left tunnels until engineer Eiji Nakatsu copied the kingfisher's beak.
The new nose made the train ten percent faster and fifteen percent more energy efficient.
What else should we steal from nature?
thumbnail_text: A BIRD FIXED THE BULLET TRAIN
first_comment: Owl feathers inspired the train's pantograph too. What invention would you copy from an animal?
